The Artemis II astronauts are now less than one hour away from splashdown, scheduled for 8:07 pm EDT (5:07 PDT) off the coast of San Diego. During reentry, the astronauts will travel faster than any humans in history, reaching speeds of roughly 24,000 miles per hour. Tune into the live broadcast of the event at the link in our bio.

Credit: NASA #artemis #moon #nasa #splashdown #artemisiiScientific American17.4K views · 5d ago0:45Artemis II just entered a brief, planned communication blackout. As the Orion capsule speeds toward earth, the capsule will be engulfed in superhot plasma, blocking communications. The blackout is expected to last six minutes. The crew is on track to splash down off the coast of San Diego, California a few minutes after 8 p.m. EDT/5 p.m. PDT today. Watch live at the link in our bio.
